# Underwriting Support Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Underwriting Support Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded files, proposed submission, document, rating and Teams connectors, and channels; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who builds, tests and later uses the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for submission, document, rating and referral connections with dedicated references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare underwriter, analyst, senior-underwriter and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, the Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Carrier rule ownership | Have the underwriting owner supply carrier-approved guidelines, tiers and rating factors to replace the fictional rules coded in the portable agent. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Manual underwriting review: how evidence is assembled per submission and where review quality varies. Agree where senior underwriters rebuild evidence instead of judging risk before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Submission | Line of business | Evidence sources | Missing items | Exceptions raised | Referred to | Decision owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Underwriting business owner | Approve scope, carrier guidelines, referral paths and success measures; keep synthetic scores and premiums out of customer results. |
| Authorized underwriters and reviewers | Own every coverage decision, with actuarial, legal, compliance and authority review where applicable. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any underwriting connection is approved. |
| Underwriting data and connection owners | Approve submission, document, rating and Teams access; record dedicated least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check UWS-01 through UWS-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject anchors that appear only in reasoning text. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route coverage questions to authorized underwriters. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for underwriting support are agreed.
- [ ] The underwriting owner records how evidence is rebuilt for each submission today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/underwriting-support/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded, with maker access granted, before any build starts.
- [ ] The authenticated underwriting audience and least-privilege scopes for applicant, loss and rating data are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/underwriting-support/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/underwriting-support/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/underwriting-support/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/underwriting-support/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Underwriting Support Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_underwriting-support-controls-and-review.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_underwriting-support-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_exception-review_04
9. Add skill: aibast_guideline-check_03
10. Add skill: aibast_pricing-recommendation_02
11. Add skill: aibast_risk-evaluation_01
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass UWS-01: Underwriter
15. Pass UWS-02: Pricing Analyst
16. Pass UWS-03: Risk Analyst
17. Pass UWS-04: Senior Underwriter
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: UWS-01, UWS-02, UWS-03, UWS-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, its smoke test calls `UnderwritingSupportAgent` and returns the required markers.
- [ ] If built manually, the Draft has the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Unchanged UWS-01 through UWS-04 prompts pass, each in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on its final answer; markers seen only in reasoning text are not proof.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing applicant, loss or rating data. Request only the read scopes the approved underwriting sources need. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 insurance submission data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting data and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 insurance submission data — read:** Bind approved read-only connector actions for submission records.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 insurance submission data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 insurance submission data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 insurance submission data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Give no legal or insurance advice; refer the question to authorized reviewers. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or coverage action succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved underwriting document repository

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting data and connection owners

1. **Bind Approved underwriting document repository — read:** Add the approved repository as a knowledge source with a content owner.

2. **Identity for Approved underwriting document repository:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved underwriting document repository:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved underwriting document repository:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Quote and bind nothing; explain the illustrative factors and loss evidence. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or coverage action succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Rating and policy-administration services

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting data and connection owners

1. **Bind Rating and policy-administration services — read:** Expose read-only rating lookups through a custom connector; keep quote, bind and policy writes unavailable.

2. **Identity for Rating and policy-administration services:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Rating and policy-administration services:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Rating and policy-administration services:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Quote and bind nothing; explain the illustrative factors and loss evidence. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or coverage action succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Teams referrals and approvals

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams referrals and approvals — write:** Gate referral workflows behind authorized underwriters (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams referrals and approvals:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams referrals and approvals:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams referrals and approvals:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 8](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send nothing; prepare the exception file and name the reviewer. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or coverage action succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting data and connection owners

Bind approved least-privilege connection references only; keep consequential actions behind explicit approval.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved submission, document, rating and referral connections replace the synthetic inputs and preserve the reviewed input and output contract.
- [ ] Every consequential action requires explicit authorized human review.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as underwriting users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic scores, tiers and premiums are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked underwriting corpus | All four cases, UWS-01 through UWS-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Regulated boundary | Any advice, quote, binder, approval, decline, policy change or coverage decision is no-go. |
| Visual evidence | Require final-answer anchors; reasoning-only and reshoot-required frames cannot pass. |
| Release state | The manual and pilot agents are Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Underwriting business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Synthetic labels, human review and no-advice, no-approval and no-transaction behavior are validated, and publication is explicitly confirmed.
- [ ] The approved underwriting audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review underwriting sessions, failed interactions, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses an eligible environment type and a supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
